text:
The scoreboard said 4-1, but the more telling number is 5.11 to 1.85 in expected goals. Tampa Bay out-chanced Philadelphia by a wide margin and, by the quality of its looks, deserved to win 84 percent of the time. Even that undersells it, since TBL put up 70 shot attempts to PHI's 37 and 36 shots on goal to 15.

Brayden Point tipped one in late in the first period, and Pontus Holmberg made it 2-0 just 17 seconds into the second. Tyson Foerster pulled PHI back within one on a 5 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night, but the Flyers never generated enough to build on it. Dan Vladar kept the game close for a long stretch, stopping 32 of 35 and saving about 1.2 goals more than the shots against him warranted.

The gap finally showed in the third, where TBL created 2.29 expected goals to PHI's 0.61. Ilya Mikheyev scored on a wrap-around at 17:00, and Brandon Hagel added an 89 percent chance at 19:53 to close it out. Hagel put eight shots on goal and carried 1.59 expected goals on his own. Nikita Kucherov finished with two assists in 22 minutes, with TBL holding a 3.08 to 0.35 edge in expected goals while he was on the ice. Andrei Vasilevskiy only had to handle 15 shots.
